newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels slaughter 23 civilians in Algeria - papers.
newsitem.headline: Rebels slaughter 23 civilians in Algeria - papers.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels killed 23 people in two attacks in Algeria, the latest in a series of massacres and killings in which about 800 civilians have died in two months, Algerian newspapers said on Wednesday.

"A terrorist gang" -- the term Algerian media and authorities use for Moslem guerrillas -- killed 19 people in Heraoua village in Ain Defla province, 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Algiers, said Al Khabar and Liberte newspapers.
The attack occured overnight Monday-Tuesday, they said. Both said they had no other details.

Four civilians were killed on Sunday when their truck was caught at a fake roadblock erected by suspected guerrillas near Ourith hamlet in the western province of Tlemcen, 440 km (275 miles) from the Algerian capital.
The rebels slashed the four people's throats, they added.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence which erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamic fundamentalists had taken a huge lead.
